items.title: Dengkil pupil's death: Education Ministry offers support
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry is providing psychosocial support to the family and school community of a Year One pupil who died after experiencing breathing difficulties in her classroom in Dengkil. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the ministry would leave the investigation to the police, with its immediate focus on supporting the family and school community. She said the Environment Ministry was monitoring the situation, while the Health Ministry would advise on the health risks.

items.title: Police record 18 statements in MCBA officer's murder probe
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Police have recorded statements from 18 people to assist investigations into the death of a Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) officer found dead at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) quarters in Nilai last Thursday. Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the investigation paper would be referred to the deputy public prosecutor in the near future. Alzafny said the post-mortem found the victim died from pressure applied to her neck, alongside three stab wounds from a sharp weapon —two to the abdomen and one to the right cheek.

items.title: Italy to send 500 troops to Milan after clashes
items.summary: ROME: Italy is preparing to send 500 troops to Milan after looting and clashes between police and mostly young protesters, with some luxury brands shutting their shops in the city. A cabinet meeting on Tuesday is expected to give the go-ahead to the deployment and approve policing powers for soldiers temporarily supporting law enforcement in the city. Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini called the clashes "shameful" and said on RTL 102.5 radio that the cabinet meeting would announce a series of "immediate measures" including the troop deployment.

items.title: PN plans appeal, premature to comment on status, says Azalina
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: It is premature to comment on Perikatan Nasional's status following its deregistration, as the coalition intends to appeal, says Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. She said questions on the matter should be directed to Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, who oversees the Registrar of Societies. Perikatan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said today that the coalition would challenge the deregistration and seek a court stay of the decision.

items.title: Israel arrests 10 after West Bank settler attacks on US photographer, French mayor
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Israeli police said Monday they had arrested 10 people in the occupied West Bank after settler attacks on an American photographer and a French mayor that drew international condemnation but mixed messages from the government. "Following the severe incidents of violence over the past weekend, including the assault of a media worker and the suspected attacks on foreign civilians, an arrest operation was conducted before dawn," said Major General Moshe Finchi, the Israeli police's West Bank commander. The Israeli human rights group Yesh Din said it documented 561 acts of settler or military violence against Palestinians since Sept 27 – more than 26 incidents a day.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds expected in 12 states, KL this evening, says MetMalaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several areas across 12 states and the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur until 6pm today. The warning also covers several areas in Perak, namely Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Muallim, Larut Matang and Selama, and in Kelantan, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu and Bachok. In Terengganu, the areas affected are Hulu Terengganu, Setiu, Dungun, Kemaman and Kuala Nerus, while in Pahang, the warning covers Jerantut, Rompin and Bentong.

items.title: MASFIH proposes nine priorities to help families of Malaysians missing in Nepal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (MASFIH) has proposed nine key priorities to address challenges faced by families of 54 Malaysians who remain missing following the Aug 26 Nepal-Tibet flood disaster. The proposals include establishing a coordinated national response mechanism, seeking urgent legal clarification from the Attorney-General's Chambers, developing a legal framework for exceptional overseas mass-disappearance cases, and obtaining official confirmation of the missing persons' status. MASFIH spokesperson Dr R. Manivannan said the proposals were presented during a meeting with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today, alongside a 29-page document outlining recommended interventions, implementation priorities and coordinated government action.

items.title: Nilai border control officer’s death: Police record statements from 18 individuals, husband remains in remand until Oct 22
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 20 — Police have recorded statements from 18 individuals to assist in investigations into the death of an officer of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), who was found dead at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) quarters in Nilai last Thursday. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the investigation paper would be referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor in the near future. Alzafny said the post-mortem found that the woman died from pressure applied to her neck.

items.title: Negri Sembilan exco removals: Govt explanation still under discussion, says Azalina
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government's response to calls for an explanation of the constitutional basis for the removal of 10 Negri Sembilan executive council (exco) members is still under discussion, says Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. She said the relevant ministry might address the matter during the winding-up of the debate in the Dewan Rakyat. Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim had earlier said that any termination of exco members without his advice had no legal effect .

items.title: [UPDATED] Muhyiddin: PN deregistration reminder to treat component parties fairly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin described the deregistration of Perikatan Nasional's registration as a reminder for coalition leaders to treat all component parties fairly. The Bersatu president said coalition leadership must also comply with the party constitution and the Societies Act 1966. Muhyiddin, who is also PN's founder, said he was saddened by the decision to cancel the coalition's registration.

items.title: Budget 2027 debate: Muhyiddin calls for urban poverty master plan, MP allocation law proposed
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Issues concerning urban poverty, the allocation of funds for Members of Parliament (MPs), and efforts to strengthen the nation’s healthcare sector were among the topics raised during the policy-level debate on the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today. The former prime minister said the plan should focus on housing, healthcare, employment, education, skills training, and social assistance to ensure that low-income groups also benefit from the nation’s economic development. He said the drafting of the act could be carried out by the Parliamentary Service Council, following the enforcement of the Parliamentary Service Act 2025.

items.title: All 242 Mara-sponsored students in France safe amid unrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) is closely monitoring the situation in France to ensure the safety and welfare of its 242 sponsored students amid ongoing unrest. Mara deputy director-general (education) Zahari Aziz said all 242 students were safe based on the latest reports from student representatives at their universities, with none reported involved in the unrest. "Mara will continue to monitor the situation, with the safety and welfare of its sponsored students remaining a top priority," he said.

items.title: Timeline: Perikatan Nasional's rise and fall
items.summary: PN's current official membership comprises Pas, Gerakan, MIPP, Parti Pejuang Tanah Air (Pejuang) and Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan). Today, RoS cancelled PN's registration. Feb 11, 2021 – Gerakan joined PN.

items.title: Sarawak steps up preparations to co-host 2027 SEA Games
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 20 — Sarawak is intensifying preparations to co-host the 2027 SEA Games from September 18 to 29 next year, with promotional activities set to continue across the state, the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly was told today. Sarawak Minister for Youth, Sports and Entrepreneur Development Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said the promotional activities include a torch run covering all 12 divisions in the state. Abdul Karim said Sarawak will host 18 of the 43 sports at the 2027 SEA Games, with dance sport newly included in the Sarawak cluster.

items.title: SME Bank to channel RM2.8bil under 2027 Budget to boost businesses
items.summary: The initiatives form part of more than RM7 billion in government-mandated programmes allocated through SME Bank's parent Bank Pembangunan Malaysia Bhd. SME Bank chief executive officer Samad Majid Zain said the initiatives will help businesses adopt technology, improve productivity, operate sustainably and expand into new markets. Another RM500 million will support tourism businesses, comprising RM200 million under the Special Fund for Tourism and RM300 million under the Tourism Programme.

items.title: Malaysia takes lead role in Asean anti-money laundering efforts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has strengthened its role in combating transnational crime after being selected as the Voluntary Lead Shepherd of the ASEAN Senior Officials Meeting on Transnational Crime (SOMTC) Working Group on Money Laundering. Awang Alik also co-chaired the Preparatory SOMTC for the 13th AMMTC Plus China Consultation, aimed at strengthening Asean-China cooperation in addressing transnational crime threats. Besides attending the 20th AMMTC, Saifuddin Nasution is scheduled to participate in four consultations with Asean dialogue partners - the 16th AMMTC Plus Three, 13th AMMTC Plus China, 11th AMMTC Plus Japan and 7th AMMTC Plus Korea.

items.title: Sabah CM: RM150m Nabawan police headquarters, housing project to begin in January 2027
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 20 — The construction of the Nabawan district police headquarters (IPD) and police housing project, with an allocation ceiling of RM150 million, is expected to begin in January 2027, said Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. He said the infrastructure project aimed to strengthen security capabilities, law enforcement and service delivery to the public, particularly in Nabawan and surrounding areas. Also present were Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, Sabah State Secretary Datuk Zainudin Aman and Sabah Police Commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun.

items.title: France vows fresh curfews as PM scrambles to restore order after riots
items.summary: PARIS: France will impose new curfews where needed on Tuesday, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said, as authorities sought to restore order after weekend demonstrations degenerated into riots. The targeted measures had "helped keep the night calm," Lecornu said. - TARGETED CURFEWS- Lecornu said that new curfews would be decided "where the situation requires it."

items.title: Malaysia looks to put durians on the fast track to China by road, rail in three to four days
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The government is stepping up negotiations with several countries in the region to facilitate the export of fresh durians to China by road and rail, with shipments expected to take just three to four days, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. He said the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM) was working closely with the Foreign Ministry and Transport Ministry to coordinate cross-border routes through Thailand, Laos, Vietnam and Cambodia. “Overland shipments are expected to take only three to four days, allowing goods, particularly durians, to reach the Chinese market quickly.

items.title: States urged to gazette over 15,000ha of public open spaces in Peninsular Malaysia, FT
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — More than 15,000 hectares or 64.47 per cent of public open spaces in Peninsular Malaysia and the Federal Territories have not yet been gazetted or are still in the process of gazettement, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. He said all state governments have been urged to expedite the gazettement of public open spaces to ensure designated green areas remain protected and are fully utilised for the benefit of the people, particularly by providing green spaces in densely populated areas. He said 23,297.15 hectares of public open spaces have been identified in Peninsular Malaysia and the Federal Territories as of December 2025.

items.title: On Israeli election eve, settler violence becomes Netanyahu liability
items.summary: ATTACKS on a US journalist and European diplomats in the occupied West Bank have turned Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's championing of settlers into a potential liability days before elections, with opponents calling him soft on "Jewish terrorism." Leading opposition contenders Gadi Eisenkot, Yair Golan and Naftali Bennett, whose politics range widely, all referred to the attacks as "Jewish terrorism" – a term of the sort that the Netanyahu government bristles at when levelled from abroad. "What is happening in the West Bank is Jewish terrorism under the auspices of the Israeli government," said centre-right candidate Eisenkot, a former military chief and Netanyahu's main rival in the Oct 27 vote.

items.title: Court sets Jan 20 for ex-TH senior manager's bribery appeal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court has fixed Jan 20 next year to hear the appeal by a former senior manager of Lembaga Tabung Haji against his conviction and sentence of three years' jail and an RM852,385 fine for accepting RM170,477 in bribes. Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin set the date during case management involving Zaharuddin Hamid, 53, a former senior manager (technical) of the Real Estate Development Section. On Nov 30, 2023, Sessions Court judge Rozina Ayob sentenced Zaharuddin to three years' imprisonment and an RM852,385 fine after finding him guilty on all three charges.

items.title: MARA says all 242 sponsored students in France safe amid unrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) is closely monitoring the situation in France to ensure the safety and welfare of its 242 sponsored students amid the unrest. In areas experiencing public transport disruptions, the universities have taken appropriate measures to conduct classes online,” he said in a statement today. “MARA would continue to monitor the situation, with the safety and welfare of its sponsored students remaining a top priority,” he added.

items.title: Queen calls for long-term measures to protect students from haze
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 20 — Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, has urged the government, private sector and local communities to take proactive, collective action to address the physical and psychological effects of haze on students and families. “Relevant parties must also develop long-term strategic plans rather than relying solely on temporary solutions when haze emergencies occur,” Her Majesty said. Her Highness Che’ Puan Mahkota Khaleeda Johor was also present.

items.title: Imported vegetable glut hurting local growers, says Mohamad
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security is working with the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti) to tackle the oversupply of imported vegetables, which is hurting local producers. He was responding to a supplementary question from Wong Shu Qi (PH-Kluang) on the need for imported vegetables and fruits to obtain good agricultural practices certification equivalent to Malaysia Good Agricultural Practices Certification Scheme (myGAP), as well as measures to protect local farmers from competition with imported produce that is not subject to the same standards. Mohamad said imported vegetables and fruits entering Malaysia were currently not required to have good agricultural practices certification equivalent to myGAP in their countries of origin, but remained subject to import requirements, including import permits, phytosanitary certificates issued by exporting countries and inspections by the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (Maqis).

items.title: Govt discusses measures to tackle glut of imported vegetables hurting local farmers
items.summary: He was responding to a supplementary question from Wong Shu Qi (PH-Kluang) on the need for imported vegetables and fruits to obtain good agricultural practices certification equivalent to Malaysia Good Agricultural Practices Certification Scheme (myGAP), as well as measures to protect local farmers from competition with imported produce that is not subject to the same standards. Mohamad said imported vegetables and fruits entering Malaysia were currently not required to have good agricultural practices certification equivalent to myGAP in their countries of origin, but remained subject to import requirements, including import permits, phytosanitary certificates issued by exporting countries and inspections by the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (MAQIS). He said commodities facing oversupply included chillies, cabbage, round cabbage, mustard greens, tomatoes and cucumbers, prompting complaints from local growers, including those in Cameron Highlands and Johor.

items.title: Ahmad Samsuri questions timing of PN deregistration
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: Perikatan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar has questioned the timing of the coalition's deregistration by the Registrar of Societies (RoS), describing the move as unusual. "All actions that coincided with the timeline leading up to the Melaka election candidate nominations, when the Election Commission (EC) had only two days earlier written to 'PN' seeking a response on the use of the 'PN' logo, clearly show a fear of this coalition," he said. RoS said the decision was made under Subparagraph 13(1)(c)(iv) of the Societies Act 1966 (Act 832), after reviewing all documents and representations submitted by PN.

items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia to expand online child safety cooperation, seek Singapore’s involvement
items.summary: BALI, Oct 20 — Malaysia and Indonesia have agreed to establish inter-agency cooperation at the implementation level to address online child safety issues, with efforts also planned to involve Singapore in the collaboration. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said online safety, particularly involving children, was an important issue requiring the collective attention of countries in the region. He said that although Asean countries have different laws and implementation approaches, the initiative by Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore could encourage other countries in the region to participate.

items.title: Mercedes-Benz Malaysia fails to strike out SUV defect lawsuits
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mercedes-Benz Malaysia Sdn Bhd has failed in its bid to have lawsuits over alleged defects in its GLE 450 4M AMG luxury sports utility vehicle (SUV) dismissed. High Court judicial commissioner Datin Zalita Zaidan upheld the lower court's decision to dismiss the company's application to strike out lawsuits brought by Beyond Natural Group Sdn Bhd and two individuals, S. Aruna and G. Hanulraj. The lawsuits concern alleged mechanical and electronic defects in the SUV, including battery failure, airbag warning malfunctions and a fire underneath a car seat.

items.title: [UPDATED] Father devastated after daughter dies following breathing emergency
items.summary: SEPANG: A father was left heartbroken after his daughter, whom he had sent to school as usual yesterday, died after reportedly suffering breathing difficulties caused by an obstructed airway. Mior Shahrizal Mior Zakaria, 48, said he rushed to Sekolah Kebangsaan Dengkil after being informed that his youngest child, Derma Damiya Nur Mikayla, was having breathing difficulties. "About 15 minutes later, the ambulance arrived, but my daughter was still completely unresponsive," he said when met at the Pekan Dengkil Muslim Cemetery here today.

items.title: Malaysia-Switzerland trade hits RM13.4bil, up 9.8pct in 2025
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia-Switzerland bilateral trade reached RM13.4 billion in 2025, an increase of 9.8 per cent from the previous year, reflecting continued growth in economic ties between the two countries. Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said that as of June, 211 manufacturing projects involving Swiss participation had been implemented in Malaysia, attracting RM12.8 billion in investments and creating 19,744 jobs. "We also discussed the Malaysia-Efta Economic Partnership Agreement (Meepa) and efforts to strengthen investment cooperation.

items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia agree to expand online safety cooperation
items.summary: BALI: Malaysia and Indonesia have agreed to establish inter-agency cooperation at the implementation level to address online child safety issues, with efforts also planned to involve Singapore in the collaboration. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said online safety, particularly involving children, was an important issue requiring the collective attention of countries in the region. Fahmi also welcomed Meutya's intention to strengthen cooperation between the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and Indonesia's Communication and Digital Affairs Ministry.

items.title: PN yet to decide logo for Melaka polls after deregistration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional has yet to decide which logo its candidates will use in the upcoming Melaka election following the coalition's deregistration by the Registrar of Societies (RoS) today. PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said it was too early to make a decision, adding that candidates could still contest under a component party's logo even without a registered coalition brand. "PN comprises Pas, Wawasan, Gerakan, Malaysian Indian People's Party (MIPP) and Pejuang.

items.title: China opposes US ban on govt agencies from using DeepSeek
items.summary: BEIJING: Beijing opposed on Tuesday a US government ban on its agencies using AI tools from Chinese startup DeepSeek, saying the move "overstretched" the concept of national security. China and the United States are locked in a race for dominance in the fast-moving artificial intelligence sector, trading accusations of stealing AI technologies and jeopardising security in recent months. The US Department of Homeland Security on Monday banned products developed by DeepSeek – and tools created using DeepSeek by third parties – saying they risked sharing sensitive data with China.

items.title: Anwar cites cases of corporate owners forced to sell firms over political interference
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The government inherited a system lacking transparency, allowing corporate crimes and market manipulation to go largely unchecked for decades, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said weaknesses in the previous system meant enforcement action was rarely taken in major cases involving billions of ringgit in losses, including corporate takeovers and banking transactions allegedly influenced by political interference. Anwar alleged that several cases involving so-called corporate mafia activities were linked to a former finance minister who wielded considerable influence and controlled substantial financial resources.

items.title: Spanish landlords feel attacked as housing crisis overshadows vote
items.summary: MADRID: Landlady Maria Jose Fernandez feels unfairly portrayed as a property speculator amid the tensions over Spain's housing crisis, just weeks before a snap nationwide election. Fernandez, a 65-year-old retiree, said the problems faced by property owners like her were being overlooked and feared government proposals to strengthen tenants' rights would make matters worse. Housing is set to feature in Spain's November 29 snap election, with landlords concerned about tighter regulations and housing activists demanding greater protection for tenants.

items.title: Policeman hurt in Tanah Merah parang attack discharged
items.summary: TANAH MERAH: A policeman who was injured in a parang attack during an anti-drug raid here on Saturday has been discharged from Tanah Merah Hospital after his condition improved. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the 37-year-old corporal was in stable condition and had been allowed to return home. He said investigations into the suspect were still ongoing.

items.title: LBS rewards homebuyers with prizes in 65th-anniversary campaign
items.summary: KULA LUMPUR: For 150 homebuyers of LBS Bina Group Bhd, the joy of owning a home came with an added reason to celebrate, as the property developer rewarded them with an array of prizes under its 65th-anniversary campaign. LBS marked the conclusion of its "Celebrate 65. Score More Than a Home" campaign with a special prize presentation ceremony, extending its anniversary celebrations to the homeowners who have been part of the group's journey.

items.title: Azalina: Teachers handling bullying cases need trauma support, counselling
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Teachers handling bullying and violence cases in schools should receive trauma management training, confidential counselling and psychological support to help them cope with the emotional toll. "We often ask how teachers can protect students. "Teachers are also human beings with feelings.

items.title: Ex-MP says army plan for migrant deportations is 'playing to the gallery'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Klang member of parliament Charles Santiago said Putrajaya MP Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin was playing to the gallery over his proposal to deploy soldiers to help deport undocumented migrants. Santiago said Malaysia should first examine how the system produced irregular migration before deploying the army. "Deploy the army?

items.title: OhBulan! Paling Viral Online returns with four new categories
items.summary: Paling Viral Online returns in November with four new categories following its inaugural edition in 2025. The second edition will feature nine categories, including Pelakon Paling Viral, Penyanyi Gen Z Paling Viral, Peniaga Paling Viral and Nepo Baby Paling Viral. Five categories from the inaugural edition will also return: Content Creator Paling Viral, Filem Paling Viral, Drama Paling Viral, Lagu Paling HOT and Kelab Peminat Paling Viral.

items.title: Malaysia-Switzerland trade hits RM13.4bil: Johari Ghani
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia-Switzerland economic ties continue to grow, with bilateral trade reaching RM13.4 billion in 2025, an increase of 9.8 per cent from the previous year. Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said as of June 2026, 211 manufacturing projects with Swiss participation had been implemented in Malaysia, involving investments worth RM12.8 billion and creating 19,744 jobs. "We also discussed the Malaysia-European Free Trade Association Economic Partnership Agreement (Meepa) and efforts to strengthen investment cooperation.

items.title: Govt to consolidate MAF veterans’ associations to improve aid distribution, says Adly Zahari
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) plans to streamline and consolidate more than 300 registered Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) veterans’ associations to facilitate the distribution of assistance to the group, said its Deputy Minister Adly Zahari. He said under the initiative, to be implemented by the National Veterans Council and the Veterans Affairs Department (JHEV), the number of associations would be reduced to 100, with the associations operating under parent associations to enable government assistance schemes to be coordinated more effectively. “We also hope the state governments will continue to support and encourage veterans’ associations, as JHEV’s focus is on ensuring the welfare of veterans,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: No quota for CLP exam passes, candidates assessed purely on merit, Dewan Rakyat told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Candidates sitting the Certificate in Legal Practice (CLP) examination are assessed purely on merit, with no quota imposed on the number of passes, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran said candidates were assessed based on their performance, with a minimum passing mark set for each subject. Candidates are assessed purely on merit,” he said during the question-and-answer session.

items.title: Loke wants Transport Expo Asia to become permanent biennial event, next edition in 2028
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke wants Transport Expo Asia (TXA) to become a permanent biennial event, with the next edition set for 2028 to showcase transport technologies and innovation. He said the exhibition would bring together industry players, promote international best practices and support the development of Malaysia’s transport industry. Loke said the idea for a dedicated transport exhibition emerged from the ministry’s co-organising of the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA).

items.title: Malaysia, WHO aim to finalise pandemic agreement by May 2027, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Malaysia and the World Health Organization (WHO) have renewed their joint commitment to finalise the landmark WHO Pandemic Agreement by May 2027, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad. He said Malaysia is emphasising the need to strike a balance between intellectual property rights protection and equitable access to medical countermeasures during health emergencies. During the meeting, he said Malaysia also reiterated its firm commitment to supporting sustainable financing for WHO.

items.title: Suhakam calls for femicide to be recognised in law, tougher action on gender-based violence
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) has urged the government to recognise femicide in the country’s legal framework. It described femicide as the most extreme form of gender-based violence against women and girls. Suhakam said “preventing femicide requires action before violence escalates into the loss of life”.

items.title: Johor-Singapore RTS Link fares expected by year-end, says transport minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Fares for the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link are expected to be announced by the end of this year, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said. The announcement will be made ahead of the service’s planned opening in February next year. “The announcement would be made jointly with RTS Operations (RTSO), as the project was a bilateral initiative between Malaysia and Singapore.

items.title: Anthony Loke: Bus ticket policy targets overseas online agents, not operators
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The government’s policy to channel bus ticket sales through licensed terminals is meant to restrict online ticketing agents (OTA). “The policy is not intended to cause losses to bus companies. In this case, Loke said, transactions will be business-to-business (B2B), between the terminals and bus operators.

items.title: Anwar says Siti Nurhaliza personally invited him to concert, praises cultural heritage showcase
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said his attendance at national songstress Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza’s concert recently was by special invitation and also in support of efforts to promote local arts, heritage and culture. Responding to criticism from several quarters over his attendance, Anwar thanked them and said he accepted their views with an open heart, according to a report by national news agency Bernama today. The prime minister said the concert by the country’s renowned singer deserved praise for elevating the nation’s cultural heritage through its various traditional elements.

items.title: Johor businessman says identity misused in fake Facebook account insulting King, Malays
items.summary: SEGAMAT, Oct 20 — A businessman has claimed that a fake Facebook account, using his name and image, was used to post content insulting the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and the Malay community. Segamat police chief Superintendent Mohd Jumazanzahir Chek Ismail said that the complainant, a local man, lodged a police report here the day before yesterday. “Police confirm having received a report regarding the misuse of his personal information to create a fake Facebook account.

items.title: Azmin: RoS deregistration shows Perikatan leadership breached coalition constitution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali said the cancellation of Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) registration showed that the coalition’s leadership, led by PAS, had breached the Societies Act 1966 and PN’s constitution. He said the PN leadership’s decision to deny Bersatu the right to attend, express its views and vote at a PN Supreme Council meeting on July 16 amounted to a serious breach of Clause 7.1 of the coalition’s constitution. Azmin said the action had caused significant harm to PN and could jeopardise its future.

items.title: Perikatan to challenge RoS deregistration, appeal to home minister, says Takiyuddin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) will challenge the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) decision to cancel the coalition’s registration, including by appealing to the home minister, its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said today. He said the legal challenge would begin with an application during the Kuala Lumpur High Court hearing of PN’s application for a stay on Thursday. Takiyuddin said PN would also take action against parties it believed had shown contempt for the court process.

items.title: Govt looking at tougher penalties to tackle cable theft across public transport sector
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Transport Ministry is in the midst of drafting necessary measures that look into increasing penalties for action against cable theft affecting public transport operators, including the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL). Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the proposed amendments would not be limited to ECRL, as cable theft was a problem affecting operators across the sector. “Proposals to increase penalties for cable theft must go through parliamentary process.

items.title: Anwar: Madani anti-money laundering enforcement actions net RM4b up to 2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Malaysian enforcement agencies have frozen up to RM4.3 billion in funds and 2.1 million shares up to 2026 as part of ongoing anti-money laundering operations, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim told Parliament today, citing police enforcement statistics. Anwar said his government has stepped up efforts to crack down on white-collar crime, which resulted in billions of ringgit seized and hundreds of prosecutions. “The total number of criminal charges has increased more than threefold,” Anwar, who is also finance minister, said during PM Question Time.

items.title: Finance Ministry halts selected pre-qualified tender method for new Rural and Regional Development Ministry projects after audit findings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Ministry of Finance (MOF) has halted approvals for the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW) to use the Selected Pre-Qualified Open Tender (TTPKT) method for new projects following findings in the Auditor-General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2025. According to the MOF, contractors for the Rural Road Programme under the KKDW are generally selected through tender processes, including open tender and the TTPKT method. According to the MOF, the original allocations approved for rural road projects under the annual budgets were RM1.09 billion in 2023, RM1.32 billion in 2024 and RM1.57 billion in 2025.

items.title: No decision yet on raising motorcycle licence age to 18, says Anthony Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The government has yet to decide whether to raise the minimum age for obtaining a motorcycle licence. Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the ministry is weighing the risk of pushing more underage riders onto the roads without valid licences. He noted that some students aged 13 or 14 were already riding motorcycles without licences despite the existing minimum age.

items.title: ECRL targets Dec 12 launch with 30pc fare discount, freight services to run concurrently, says Anthony Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) will offer a 30 per cent discount on Economy Transit and Express fares for the first month of operations. The Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) is targeting December 12 for the start of services, with ticket sales expected to begin in mid-November, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said after launching the Transport Expo Asia 2026 here today. Freight operations to begin alongside passenger services When asked on freight operations between Gombak and Kota Bharu, Loke said they are expected to begin alongside passenger services, allowing the railway to serve both passenger and cargo transport needs.

items.title: Border agency chief Shuhaily to face court tomorrow over alleged assault of two police personnel
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain has confirmed that he will appear at the Sepang Magistrate’s Court tomorrow to face a charge of assaulting two police personnel. Mohd Shuhaily said he was prepared to face the country’s legal process and accept whatever decision the court made in the case. Meanwhile, Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, when contacted, confirmed that Mohd Shuhaily would be charged with two counts under Section 323 of the Penal Code.

items.title: Anwar says SC pursued fresh Serba Dinamik charges under Madani, AG task force report to be made public within three months
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim told Parliament today that the Securities Commission (SC) pursued further action in the corporate scandal involving Serba Dinamik Berhad, leading to new charges in early 2026. Anwar said the SC had initially charged Serba Dinamik and its managing director, Datuk Mohd Abdul Karim Abdullah, in December 2021 over false statements submitted to Bursa Malaysia. “Under the Madani administration, the SC pursued investigations into other transactions involving Datuk Karim.
